steps.intro: Listen for the quick “e” of the shewa, and for the throat letters א ה ח ע.

cards.title: The shewa ְ: a quick e, or nothing
body: Two dots one above the other under a letter are a shewa. Sometimes you say it as a very short e; sometimes it is silent and just shows the letter has no vowel.

Said: at the start of a word, as in דְּבָרִים, de-va-RIM. Silent: at the end of a syllable, as in מִדְבָּר, mid-BAR. When two shewas stand side by side in the middle of a word, the first is silent and the second is said.

examples.en: words: the shewa starts the word, so say it
wilderness: the shewa closes “mid”, so it's silent

cards.title: The throat letters: א ה ח ע (and ר)
body: These letters are made at the back of the throat, and it shows in the spelling. They never take a plain said shewa: instead they take a shewa with a short vowel beside it, ֲ ֱ ֳ (a, e, o). Grammar books call these hateph vowels.
They like the a-vowels: נַעַר has patah under both throat letters.
And they can't be doubled, so they never take the doubling dot. Lesson 7 shows what happens when “the” would double one.

cards.title: A sneaky a, and letters that go quiet
body: When ח or ע ends a word after another vowel, a patah is slipped in under it and said first: רוּחַ is RU-ach, not ru-cha. This is called a furtive patah.
א at the end of a syllable makes no sound: לֹא is just lo. ה at the end of a word is usually silent too, as in תּוֹרָה, to-RAH.

examples.en: say the a before the ch

cards.prompt: In מִדְבָּר (wilderness), the shewa under ד is…
options: silent: it closes the syllable mid
cards.explain: It ends the syllable mid, so it is silent: mid-BAR.

cards.prompt: In דְּבָרִים (words), the first shewa is…
cards.explain: A shewa at the start of a word is always said: de-va-RIM.

cards.prompt: Match each hateph vowel to its sound.
Why does אֲנִי (I) have ֲ and not a plain shewa ְ?
options: א is a throat letter, and they take the hateph vowels
It is the first word of a sentence
cards.explain: Throat letters can't carry a plain said shewa, so they take ֲ, ֱ or ֳ instead.
A furtive patah is said before its letter: RU-ach.

steps.intro: Look for shewas, said and silent, and the throat letters with their hateph vowels.

cards.note: Near the end, וְרוּחַ אֱלֹהִים: “and the Spirit of God”. רוּחַ has its furtive patah, and אֱלֹהִים starts with hateph segol.
The last word is אֱמֶת, truth: “and your law is truth”.
